q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm, AE = 4 cm. Find EC.
q.e: A line parallel to one side cuts the other two in the same ratio (BPT): 2/3 = 4/EC, so EC = 6.

q.t: Two similar triangles have sides in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their areas?
q.e: Area grows with length × length, so the area ratio is the square of the side ratio.

q.t: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
q.e: Pythagoras: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100 = 10².

q.t: Is a triangle with sides 7, 24, 25 right-angled?
o: No — the sides are not in proportion
q.e: 49 + 576 = 625 = 25², and by the converse of Pythagoras that forces a right angle.

q.t: Which triangles are ALWAYS similar to each other?
q.e: Every equilateral triangle has angles 60°, 60°, 60°, so any two match by AA.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB = 4 cm, PQ = 8 cm and BC = 5 cm. Find QR.
q.e: Corresponding sides are in one ratio: PQ/AB = 2, so QR = 2 × 5.

q.t: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar by…
q.e: Two equal angles force the third to be equal too (sum 180°), so the shape is fixed.

q.t: A 10 m ladder leans on a wall with its foot 6 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
q.e: The ladder is the hypotenuse: √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8.

q.t: Two similar triangles have areas 25 cm² and 49 cm². What is the ratio of their corresponding sides?
q.e: Areas are in the square of the side ratio, so take square roots: √25 : √49.

q.t: The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles equals the ratio of their…
q.e: Each side is scaled by the same factor, so their sum (the perimeter) is scaled by that factor too.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC. AD/DB = 3/5 and AC = 5.6 cm. Find AE.
q.e: AD/DB = 3/5 means AE is 3 of 8 equal parts of AC: 3/8 × 5.6.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = x, DB = x − 3, AE = x + 3 and EC = x − 2. Find x.
q.e: BPT: x/(x − 3) = (x + 3)/(x − 2). Cross-multiply: x² − 2x = x² − 9, so x = 4.5.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with areas 64 cm² and 121 cm². EF = 15.4 cm. Find BC.
A rhombus has diagonals 24 cm and 10 cm. Find its side.
q.e: Diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, making right triangles with legs 12 and 5.

q.t: Find the height of an equilateral triangle of side 12 cm.
q.e: The height bisects the base: √(12² − 6²) = √108 = 6√3.

q.t: A 6 m pole casts a 4 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 28 m shadow. How tall is the tower?
q.e: Sun rays make the same angle, so the triangles are similar: height/shadow = 6/4, so 28 × 1.5.

q.t: In ΔABC, AD bisects ∠A and meets BC at D. AB = 6, AC = 9, BC = 10. Find BD.
q.e: The angle bisector splits BC in the ratio AB : AC = 2 : 3, so BD = 2/5 × 10.

q.t: D, E, F are the midpoints of the sides of ΔABC. What is ar(DEF) : ar(ABC)?
q.e: Each side of DEF is half a side of ABC (midpoint theorem), so the areas are in (1/2)² = 1/4.

q.t: In ΔABC, AB = 6√3 cm, AC = 12 cm and BC = 6 cm. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: AB² + BC² = 108 + 36 = 144 = AC², so by the converse of Pythagoras the angle opposite AC, which is ∠B, is 90°.

q.t: Two poles of heights 6 m and 11 m stand 12 m apart. Find the distance between their tops.
q.e: Make a right triangle: horizontal 12, vertical 11 − 6 = 5. √(144 + 25) = 13.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at A and AD ⊥ BC. BD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm. Find AD.
q.e: The altitude to the hypotenuse makes two similar triangles, giving AD² = BD × DC = 36.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at A and AD ⊥ BC with BD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm. Find AB.
q.e: ΔABD ~ ΔCBA gives AB² = BD × BC = 4 × 13 = 52, so AB = 2√13.

q.t: Two cars leave the same point: one goes north at 30 km/h, the other east at 40 km/h. How far apart are they after 2 hours?
q.e: They have gone 60 km and 80 km along perpendicular roads, so the gap is √(60² + 80²) = 100.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and ar(ABC) = 4 × ar(PQR). If BC = 12 cm, find QR.
q.e: The area ratio 4 means the side ratio is √4 = 2, so QR = 12 ÷ 2.

q.t: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC and AB = 2 DC. The diagonals meet at O. Find ar(AOB) : ar(COD).
q.e: ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (alternate angles), with side ratio AB : CD = 2 : 1, so areas are 4 : 1.

q.t: Equilateral triangles are drawn on a side and on a diagonal of a square. What is the ratio of their areas (side : diagonal)?
q.e: The diagonal is √2 × side; areas of similar shapes go as length², so (√2)² = 2.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC and AD : DB = 2 : 3. Find ar(ADE) : ar(trapezium BCED).
q.e: AD : AB = 2 : 5, so ar(ADE) : ar(ABC) = 4 : 25. The trapezium is the rest: 25 − 4 = 21.

q.t: A girl 1.5 m tall walks away from the foot of a 4.5 m lamp-post at 1.2 m/s. How long is her shadow after 5 seconds?
q.e: She is 6 m from the post. Similar triangles: 1.5/s = 4.5/(6 + s), so 4.5s = 9 + 1.5s and s = 3.

q.t: AD is an altitude of an equilateral triangle ABC. AD² is what fraction of AB²? (Give a decimal.)
q.e: D is the midpoint of BC, so AD² = AB² − (AB/2)² = 3/4 AB².

q.t: Two similar triangles have areas 81 cm² and 49 cm². A median of the larger is 6.3 cm. Find the corresponding median of the smaller.
q.e: All corresponding lengths go in the side ratio √(49/81) = 7/9: 6.3 × 7/9.

q.t: In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. P lies on CA and Q on CB. AQ² + BP² equals…
q.e: AQ² = AC² + CQ² and BP² = BC² + CP². Regroup: (AC² + BC²) + (CP² + CQ²) = AB² + PQ².

q.t: In equilateral ΔABC, D on BC has BD = BC/3. AD² is what fraction of AB²?
q.e: Drop the altitude AE (E the midpoint). DE = a/2 − a/3 = a/6 and AE² = 3a²/4, so AD² = 3a²/4 + a²/36 = 28a²/36.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC and ar(ADE) = ar(trapezium DECB). Find AD : AB.
q.e: ar(ADE) is half of ar(ABC). Area ratio 1/2 means side ratio √(1/2).

q.t: In ΔABC, AB = 8, AC = 6, BC = 10 and AD is the median to BC. Find AD.
q.e: 6² + 8² = 10², so ∠A = 90°. The midpoint of the hypotenuse is equally far from all three vertices, so AD = 10/2.

q.t: A 15 m ladder reaches a 12 m high window on one side of a street. Turned over, it reaches a 9 m high window on the other side. How wide is the street?
q.e: Its foot is √(225 − 144) = 9 m from one wall and √(225 − 81) = 12 m from the other: 9 + 12.

q.t: Two similar triangles have areas 100 cm² and 64 cm². The altitude of the smaller is 6.4 cm. Find the corresponding altitude of the larger.
ΔABC is right-angled at B and D is the midpoint of BC. AC² equals…
q.e: AC² = AB² + (2CD)² and AD² = AB² + CD². Subtract: AC² − AD² = 3CD².

q.t: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and the diagonals meet at O. AO = 3x − 1, OC = 5x − 3, BO = 2x + 1, OD = 6x − 5. Find x.
q.e: Parallel sides make AO/OC = BO/OD. Cross-multiplying gives 2x² − 5x + 2 = 0, so x = 2 or 1/2; x = 1/2 makes OC negative.

q.t: A rhombus has diagonals 16 cm and 30 cm. Find its perimeter.
q.e: Half-diagonals 8 and 15 meet at right angles, so a side is √(64 + 225) = 17; four sides = 68.

q.t: A right triangle has legs 15 cm and 20 cm. Find the length of the perpendicular from the right angle to the hypotenuse.
q.e: Hypotenuse = 25. Twice the area two ways: 15 × 20 = 25 × p, so p = 12.
